ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $C$ is a moving point on line segment $BD$, with perpendiculars $AB \perp BD$ and $ED \perp BD$ drawn through points $B$ and $D$, respectively. The lines $AC$ and $EC$ are also drawn. Given that $AB=5$, $DE=1$, and $BD=8$, and letting $CD=x$, what is the minimum value of $AC+CE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram: \\
When points A, C, and E are collinear, AC + CE is minimized;\\
When points A, C, and E are on the same line,\\
extend AB and construct line EF $\perp$ AB at point F,\\
$\because$AB = 5, DE = 1,\\
$\therefore$AF = 6,\\
$\because$$\angle$ABD = $90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$FBD = $90^\circ$,\\
$\because$$\angle$BDE = $\angle$BFE = $90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$Quadrilateral BFED is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore$BD = EF = 8,\\
$\therefore$AE = $ \sqrt{AF^{2} + EF^{2}}$ = $ \sqrt{6^{2} + 8^{2}}$ = \boxed{10}.
